validated_work_order.understanding: All three follow-ups from #44 reproduce on main as filed, and all three are kept. (1) Review: the fixture guard in the #44 test (test/web/pages.test.js, the 'seeded' assertion before the render loop, at line 1017-1020) filters the appended rows on event_type === 'lead_qualified' and asserts a count of 1 — the denominator only. The spend.observed row that carries 3_000_000_000 is the numerator and is unguarded, so a fixture that stops carrying the amount still passes the guard and then fails at the CPL assertion with 'Qualified CPL in dollars on the ideal branch, got —', which reads as a currency regression. (2) Review: the same test re-creates the tenant_usd + opp_usd_expensive block ('opp_usd_expensive' occurs 4 times, in two identical create blocks at 931-940 and 978-988) and the seven-line `envelope` closure ('const envelope = (event_id' occurs 3 times, at 295, 339 and 1001) that already exists twice more in the file, differing only in the tenant_id literal. freshRepos()/seededRepos() at 24 and 30 are the file's established idiom for this. The reviewer's own note says the fence around the two existing USD tests belongs to whoever owns the order — that is this order, and it is lifted deliberately. (3) QA: ISO_CURRENCIES.includes is exact, so a tenant row holding 'usd', 'Usd' or ' USD ' never resolves. I reproduced this against main and it is WORSE than the report says, so the 'minor' severity does not stand. Measured on the shipped seed with tenant_demo set to 'usd': /opportunities first row reads 'value ₹6,000.00' (as reported) and the page carries six rupee amounts, / carries six, /experiments carries four, the Qualified CPL tile reads '—', GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0 with qualified_cpl_micros null, and POST /v1/events 400s CURRENCY_MISMATCH on a legitimate USD spend. Same for 'Usd' and ' USD ' — byte-identical pages, measured. The blast radius is still narrow and the trigger is external: normaliseGrowthEvent validates ingest currency against ISO_CURRENCIES exactly on both the body.value path and the pre-normalised payload path (src/domain/measurement.js:124 and :136), and routes.js seeds a new tenant's currency from that validated code, so nothing the app itself writes today produces a non-canonical code. The bug is that the read path is not defensive about a row it did not write (a human UPDATE, a legacy import, a future write path). THE CORRECTION CARRIED SINCE v1, restated because the last two reviews each showed it is the easiest thing to get wrong: the em-dash on the SHIPPED SEED is not the defect and this order does not claim it is. The seed's only spend row (evt_seed_journey_spend_1) carries currency 'INR', amount_micros 7_200_000_000 (scripts/seed.js:21-25), and there are three seeded lead_qualified rows (:41-55). So a tenant whose spend rows are all genuinely foreign correctly sums to nothing and correctly renders the em-dash — that is computeFunnel's foreign-currency exclusion working (QA BUG-2), not a canonicalisation failure. What the defect removes is the case where the tenant's own unit of account and its own spend agree and the spend is merely LABELLED differently from the row: there the exclusion drops the tenant's real spend, the CPL goes null, and the ingest path 400s a legitimate event. v3 was rejected for exactly one reason and this version answers it directly: AC-6 and qa_script step 10 pinned `grep -c "const envelope = (event_id" test/web/pages.test.js` to 1 while the same work order's tests[] renamed that very closure to `validatedEnvelope(tenantId, ...)`, so the string the criterion greps for would not exist in the refactored file and the count would print 0 — a criterion whose own how_to_verify measures the number it forbids. The objection is mechanically correct and I did not dispute it. v4 keeps the design untouched (the objection was about the work order's arithmetic, not about canonicalising the stored row) and rewrites AC-6, tests[]'s refactor case and qa_script step 10 as one consistent set of four greps, each with its exact command and its exact expected count, so the criterion keeps proving 'exactly one closure, reached through a helper' and not merely 'the old name is gone'.
validated_work_order.root_cause: One exact-match membership test standing in for currency identity, at every point where a STORED TENANT code is read. A tenant code is stored as an arbitrary string (tenants.create takes any string; the column is TEXT), but three consumers compare it by exact string equality: money()'s ISO_CURRENCIES.includes guard at src/web/pages.js:222, computeFunnel's tenant-currency exclusion as fed from src/web/pages.js:377 and src/api/routes.js:170-171, and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check at src/api/routes.js:145-150. 'usd' and 'USD' name the same unit of account, so all three treat the tenant's own spend as foreign and either relabel it or drop it. Nothing canonicalises between the row and those comparisons. The asymmetry that makes the fix safe: the tenant row is the only untrusted side of every one of these comparisons. The other side — an event's payload currency — is already canonical, because normaliseGrowthEvent rejects anything outside ISO_CURRENCIES exactly before the row is ever compared to it. So canonicalise the stored row, never the event payload, and never inside computeFunnel.
validated_work_order.approach: Add one exported boundary function to the domain — canonicalCurrency(code) in src/domain/money.js, which trims and upper-cases a stored string and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none ('ZZZ' and 'XTS' still resolve to null, so the documented bad-data INR fallback and the never-500 behaviour are unchanged). Then resolve every read of a tenant row's currency through it, in one seam per module, rather than touching the comparisons individually: pages.js gets a local tenantCurrency(tenant) helper used at all EIGHT `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` / `tenant.currency ?? 'INR'` read sites (measured on main: 326, 346, 377, 390, 744, 758, 833, 849), and money() itself canonicalises before the fallback so any value that reaches the renderer by another path still draws its own unit. routes.js gets a local resolveTenantCurrency(row) helper used at both reads of the row — the metrics funnel filter and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check — with the comparison canonicalising while the 400's message and details keep reporting the stored string verbatim, so every existing 400 is byte-identical and only the mis-cased tenant changes from rejected to accepted. The name is resolveTenantCurrency and not tenantCurrency deliberately: src/api/routes.js:170 already declares `const tenantCurrency = ...` inside the metrics handler, and a same-named module function would be shadowed there and a self-referential `const tenantCurrency = tenantCurrency(row)` would throw a TDZ ReferenceError. computeFunnel is NOT changed: it keeps its exact string comparison and is simply fed a canonical code, because its event-payload side is already guaranteed canonical by ingest. That is also what keeps the QA BUG-2 foreign-currency exclusion intact — a 'usd' tenant must still exclude a genuinely INR spend row, and a new test now pins that so a future implementer cannot 'fix' the em-dash by summing foreign spend; AC-4 makes the same exclusion observable at a live URL. Read-side only, deliberately: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never touches tenants.create, so a write-side fix would not have fixed the reported case; and the existing test at test/web/pages.test.js:1078-1081 pins tenants.create accepting any string, so tightening the write path would break a deliberate contract for no gain on the reported defect. Separately, close the two review findings in the same test file: lift the repeated tenant+opportunity block into a usdRepos() helper beside freshRepos()/seededRepos() and the repeated envelope closure into one tenant-parameterised validatedEnvelope(), and have all three call sites use them; and extend the fixture guard to assert the resolved spend amount alongside the qualified-lead count, so a broken numerator fails at the guard with a fixture-shaped message instead of surfacing at the money assertion as an em-dash.

files.change: Export a new canonicalCurrency(currency): trims and upper-cases a stored code and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none (non-string, empty/whitespace, or an unknown code like 'ZZZ' or 'XTS'). Implementation: `export function canonicalCurrency(currency) { if (typeof currency !== 'string') return null; const code = currency.trim().toUpperCase(); return ISO_CURRENCIES.includes(code) ? code : null; }`. Document why case and whitespace are not currency errors and why a genuinely unknown code is still a data error. Leave assertValidCurrency strict — fromMicros/toMicros' contract stays 'a code I can render', and loosening it would change the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins. The new function is the read-time boundary for a STORED row, not a second constructor and not a normaliser for event payloads (those are validated exactly at ingest already).

cases: canonicalCurrency resolves an already-canonical code to itself: 'USD' -> 'USD', 'INR' -> 'INR'
canonicalCurrency resolves a mis-cased code: 'usd' -> 'USD', 'Usd' -> 'USD', 'uSd' -> 'USD'
canonicalCurrency resolves a padded code: ' USD ' -> 'USD', '\nINR\t' -> 'INR'

canonicalCurrency returns null for a code that names no ISO currency: 'ZZZ' -> null, and also 'Xts' -> null (a non-national code stays an error even when normalised — ISO_CURRENCIES deliberately omits the fund codes)
canonicalCurrency returns null without throwing for a non-string: undefined, null, 42, {}, and for '' and '   '
assertValidCurrency is unchanged: fromMicros(1, 'usd') still throws INVALID_CURRENCY — the new function is a read-time boundary, not a second constructor

acceptance.check: After a USD spend.observed of 3_000_000_000 micros is accepted for the 'usd' tenant, the Qualified CPL tile on / reads '$1,000.00' and must not read '—'. The arithmetic, which is the whole content of this criterion: the tenant's own USD spend is 3_000_000_000 micros (the seeded INR spend row of 7_200_000_000 stays excluded — that exclusion is correct and must NOT change, and AC-4 checks it), qualified_volume is 3 (the three seeded lead_qualified rows; the step appends no lead), so 3_000_000_000 / 3 = 1_000_000_000 micros = $1,000.00. The invariant is spend_micros / qualified_volume, so this figure holds only for a step that appends exactly one USD spend and no lead; appending a lead as well would make it $750.00, and that is a different criterion, not this one. What the defect removes is that on main the POST that creates this situation is itself a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH, so the tile cannot be given a number at all. Note for the reader: the '$3,000.00' in test/web/pages.test.js is a DIFFERENT fixture (a fresh database, one qualified lead, no seed rows) and deliberately does not match this one.

qa_script: Set the environment up ONCE, so the seed and the server provably share one database file: `export PORT=3100` then `export DB_PATH=$(mktemp -d)/qa58.db`, then `npm run sdlc:seed`, then `node src/index.js &`, then retry `curl -fsS localhost:$PORT/health` until it returns 200. Confirm the seed and the serve agree before going further: `sqlite3 $DB_PATH 'SELECT id,currency FROM tenants;'` must print exactly one row, `tenant_demo|INR`. Every later UPDATE below is written as `sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE ...; SELECT changes();"` and MUST print 1 — a 0 means the wrong DB_PATH, and the run is void rather than passed. (If you use `npm run sdlc:serve` instead of `node src/index.js`, remember it is the same process; the point of the check above is that the two agree.)

Orientation only — the shipped seed at its own INR, which this ticket does NOT change. Measured on unmodified main in exactly this state: /opportunities first row reads 'value ₹6,000.00'; / draws seven rupee amounts (six in the Meta tables — ₹500.00, ₹1,000.00, ₹250.00, ₹4,000.00, ₹8,750.00, ₹1,250.00 — plus the CPL tile's ₹2,400.00); /experiments draws four; GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 7200000000, qualified_volume 3, qualified_cpl_micros 2400000000; and POSTing a USD spend.observed to tenant_demo is a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with details {tenant_currency:'INR', received:'USD'}, which is correct — an INR tenant must not take USD spend. `sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency = 'usd' WHERE id = 'tenant_demo'; SELECT changes();"` — must print 1. THIS is the step that creates the defective state. Reload /opportunities: the first [data-testid=opportunity-row] (data-opportunity-id='opp_seed_expensive') must read 'value $6,000.00' and 'cost $1,900.00'. risks: money() is the last line before a number reaches a reader, so its fallback now depends on canonicalCurrency. A code that resolves to a real ISO currency but whose MINOR_EXPONENTS entry is missing (a 0- or 3-digit currency such as JPY or BHD) now renders where it previously fell back to INR. That is the correct unit, and microsPerMinorUnit already defaults to 2 for those, so the split maths is unchanged — but it is a real behaviour change for any tenant whose code is a valid non-2-exponent currency written in lower case, and it is the intended fix.

Relaxing the ingest mismatch check means a 'usd' tenant now accepts USD spend it used to reject. That is the point, but it is the one place where this order makes the write path more permissive, so the genuine-mismatch controls in the tests, in AC-3 and in qa_script steps 7 and 8 matter: a 'USD' tenant + EUR spend, and a 'ZZZ' tenant + USD spend, must both still 400 with the stored string reported verbatim.

The temptation this ticket creates is the one two rounds of review have now caught: reading the em-dash as the bug and 'fixing' it by making computeFunnel sum foreign-currency spend. That would break QA BUG-2, which is the reason the exclusion exists. The fix is to canonicalise the stored tenant row, never the event payload and never the comparison inside computeFunnel. Three things now hold that line in place — the negative unit case in tests[], the live spend_micros check in step 6 ($1,000.00, not $3,400.00) and the second-database em-dash in step 9 — so a build that widens the exclusion fails the run instead of shipping.

The CURRENCY_MISMATCH error's message and details keep the stored string verbatim, so an operator with a 'usd' row who now gets a 202 sees no message at all; the canonicalisation is silent by design. Accepted: the row is bad data, the numbers are right, and no in-app write path produces the row.

Changing the seed's spend row to be USD-denominated, so that the bare seeded database would show a dollar CPL for a 'usd' tenant. Making computeFunnel canonicalise the event payload currency, or comparing currencies there with anything other than exact equality. alternatives_considered.approach: Canonicalise in tenants.create on write, coercing the stored row to its canonical form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not fix the reported repro, which sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE and never reaches the repository. It would also break the contract test/web/pages.test.js:1078-1081 pins — that tenants.create accepts any string and a page render must not 500 on bad data — and it would silently rewrite operator-supplied data. Read-side canonicalisation covers every source of a bad row, which is a superset of what write-side covers.

alternatives_considered.approach: Reject the non-canonical code at the render boundary: keep the INR fallback but return an error panel or an unformatted 'USD 6,000.00' when the stored code is merely mis-cased.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The money() doc comment already argues the opposite trade deliberately — a correctly-formatted amount in the repo default over a mislabelled-but-honest one. And the honest-label option does not help here: 'usd' is not bad data in the way 'ZZZ' is, it is the same currency with different typing, and a reader seeing 'USD 6,000.00' instead of '$6,000.00' learns nothing was wrong.

alternatives_considered.approach: Loosen assertValidCurrency in money.js so fromMicros itself accepts and normalises 'usd', and let the three comparison sites stay as they are.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the money constructor's contract rather than its consumers, so the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins moves for every caller, and it still does not fix computeFunnel's tenant-currency comparison, which is a string compare with no money constructor in it. The defect is at the read boundary, so that is where the fix belongs.

alternatives_considered.approach: Verify the CPL fix by rewriting the seeded spend row's currency in place: UPDATE raw_events SET payload = json_set(payload,'$.currency','USD').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is not available: raw_events carries the raw_events_append_only_update trigger, and the seeded data is append-only by design (TR-20). This is also why the em-dash control needs a second database rather than an edit — the same fact the earlier review objection turned on. The fixture has to arrive through ingest, which is the path the ticket is about anyway.

The number is $1,000.00, with the arithmetic in AC-2 and the counterfactual $3,400.00 in AC-4.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The state is unreachable on that database by construction, not merely inconvenient: the em-dash needs a tenant whose only spend is foreign, and once step 4's USD row is in an append-only table every currency admits one of the two rows. alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the currency defect in this ticket and file findings 1 and 2 as a separate cleanup issue.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket bundles them on purpose and the reviewer's own note on finding 2 asks for the fixture lift to be owned by whoever holds the order. All three land in test/web/pages.test.js plus the currency path that file guards, and the new canonicalisation test wants the very helper findings 1 and 2 ask for. Splitting would mean the helper lands in one PR and the test that uses it in another.

alternatives_considered.approach: Answer the v3 objection by renaming the lifted helper back to something the existing grep still matches, so AC-6's original count of 1 survives unchanged.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That contorts the source to fit the check. The objection's own required form is the better one: grep for the OLD name at 0 and the NEW name at 1, which proves the stronger claim ('exactly one closure, reached through a helper') instead of only 'the old string still appears once'. A criterion whose required count is satisfied by keeping a vestigial un-invoked copy of the old closure is a weaker gate, and this criterion is the only mechanical proof the refactor happened.

assumptions: Trim-and-upper is the right canonicalisation for ISO 4217 codes, and no tenant needs a code that is legitimately mixed-case or padded. ISO 4217 codes are upper-case alpha-3 by definition, so the mapping is total on well-formed input and a no-op on canonical input.

A mis-cased or padded tenant code is bad data, not a distinct unit of account, and no tenant row anywhere in the wild holds a code that canonicalises to something other than what was meant. The only sources are a human UPDATE and a legacy import; the app's own write path already emits canonical codes.

The stored tenant row is the only side of every currency comparison that needs canonicalising. The event-payload side is validated exactly at ingest on both paths into the payload, so there is no second untrusted spelling to handle.
unknowns: Whether any deployed database outside this repo holds a non-canonical tenant row. Nothing in the repo enumerates tenants beyond the demo one, and the read-side fix makes such a row render correctly whether or not it exists, so the answer does not change the work — it changes only whether QA ever sees the bug in the wild.

Whether a tenant row could ever legitimately hold a currency outside ISO_CURRENCIES that this build should still render. The 'ZZZ' test says no: unknown is bad data and INR is the documented fallback. This ticket does not revisit that decision, and qa_script step 7 keeps that control live. One measured consequence to be aware of: a 'ZZZ' tenant's GET /v1/metrics spend_micros changes from 0 on main to 7_200_000_000 after the fix, because the fallback is now applied consistently to the metric as well as to the renderer — so AC-3 deliberately asserts no metrics number at 'ZZZ'.
residual_risks: A stored code that is mis-cased AND a currency with no 2-digit minor unit now renders in its own unit for the first time, where before it drew rupees. If any such row exists, the numbers a reader sees will change currency on upgrade. That is the fix, not a regression, and no test asserts the old value for such a row — but QA should read the first AC-1 render as a deliberate change rather than a diff to be accepted at a glance.

A non-canonical row stays non-canonical in storage after this change. It renders correctly everywhere now, but the next reader of the tenants table sees 'usd' and may reasonably assume the app normalises on write. It does not. The fix is stated at the read boundary in the money() doc comment, which is the only place a future implementer is likely to be looking.

Because raw_events is append-only, an operator who realises a tenant row is mis-cased cannot repair the affected spend rows once they have been written in the wrong unit — the events stay foreign and stay excluded, and the CPL stays null. The read-side fix makes such a row render its own currency for everything else, so the remaining wrongness is confined to the funnel, and correcting it means new events rather than an edit. This is a property of the existing append-only design, not something this change introduces, and it is a reason the silent canonicalisation is acceptable rather than a reason to widen the ticket.
